newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans call TV programme to say lack info on euro.
newsitem.headline: Germans call TV programme to say lack info on euro.

text.p: About 95 percent of some 19,000 people who called in to a German television programme on Tuesday about the new European currency said they lacked sufficient information about the planned euro, a television network said on Wednesday.

Germany's ARD network said 19,068 people responded to a request on the programme to express their views on the future single European currency, with 18,124 saying they were insufficiently informed about the euro slated to begin in January 1999.
Only 944 people, or five percent, said that they felt sufficiently informed, ARD said in a statement.

Former Bundesbank President Karl Otto Poehl was a guest on the programme to discuss the new currency, which will bind together those European countries that meet criteria laid out in the Maastricht Treaty for membership.
